answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks when each identity locks a refundable stake before transacting, then earns signed receipts by completing small verifiable tasks checked by random peers. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust with no credit and must pay work over time; reputation accrues only from a hash-chained ledger of verified output, so the lagoon of cheap throwaway identities stays shallow: each fake locks its own stake and passes real checks. The vertex of full participation needs a chain of verified receipts, and one forged receipt breaks the chain and slashes the deposit.
